newsitem.title: USA: Gemstar shrs hurt after EPS view cut.
newsitem.headline: Gemstar shrs hurt after EPS view cut.

text.p: Gemstar International Group Ltd shares lost their footing Thursday after being slapped by Alex. Brown with an earnings estimate reduction, Nasdaq traders said.
In afternoon Nasdaq trade, the shares tumbled more than 30 percent, or 6-3/8, to 14-3/4 on volume about five times the average daily volume.
While Alex. Bown analyst Steven Eskenazi was not immediately available to comment, a source at the firm confirmed the reduction in estimates.
The company is most noted for its VCR Plus technology that facilitates the automatic recording of television programming on video cassette recorders.
With Thursday's decline, the shares approached the $12 per share initial public offering price. The November, 1995 IPO was managed by Alex. Brown.
A secondary offering of 2.6 million shares, 300,000 from the company and also managed by Alex. Brown, occurred last April at a price of $25.25 per share.
Gemstar's year-high share price of 41-3/4 was notched one year ago, on November 9, 1995.
Gemstar on Wednesday reported fiscal second quarter earnings of $0.13 per share, or $4.3 million, versus $0.09, or $2.4 million, one year ago.
Revenues for the three months ended September 30 rose to $13.1 million from $11.2 million.
